subject: Integracare MAP: perf eval plan and close timeline
messages:
From: Tom Wilson <tom.wilson@integracare.com>

Cc: integracare-ops@integracare.com
Date: 2026-11-27T15:08:00-05:00
Subject: Integracare MAP kickoff + perf targets

Laura —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. We want to formalize a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) so we can align the evaluation matrix and the close timeline. High level asks from our side: 
- TTFT (time to first token) target: <= 250ms P50; ideally P95 < 400ms
- End-to-end P95 latency for 1.5k token clinical summaries: < 600ms
- Sustained concurrency target: 80 active sessions with bounded tail latency
- Throughput goal: support 40 concurrent sessions generating ~150 tokens each (workload approx. 6k tokens/sec aggregate)

We understand tradeoffs between model size/quality and latency. For decisioning we need a clear eval plan that includes: test dataset (de-identified clinical notes), quality metric (ROUGE/clinical-extraction F1), and per-variant perf numbers (TTFT/P50/P95, tokens/sec at target concurrency).

Can you send a MAP draft that includes a recommended model variant sweep, a proposed test harness and timeline to close (we're targeting contract signature by Dec 15 if tests look good)? Also note Integracare security will want the SOC2 artifact; I'll loop them in after we have the eval plan.

Tom
Director, Digital Innovation
Integracare Health

Attachments: none
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Tom —

Appreciate the clarity on targets. Attached is a first-draft MAP and an evaluation runbook (Integracare_MAP_v1.xlsx). High level summary below so your team can review quickly.

Mutual Action Plan (summary)
- Goal: validate model/serving configuration that meets clinical-quality bar and operational SLOs (TTFT, P95 latency, concurrency).
- Timeline: 2-week execution window for perf+quality sweep. Blocked items: de-identified eval set + SOC2 artifact for deployment (we can provision a dedicated test VPC).
- Decision gates: quality pass (F1>=0.82 on extraction + clinician spot-check) AND perf pass (P95<=600ms at 80 concurrency or acceptable fallback config).

Evaluation plan (runbook)
- Dataset: 1,200 de-identified clinical notes (sampling across specialties), 600 holdout for quality scoring.
- Metrics: TTFT (ms), latency P50/P95/P99 (ms), tokens/sec (aggregate & per-session), throughput (sessions/sec), quality F1/Rouge-L, token-level hallucination checks.
- Load profile: stepped concurrency at 10/25/50/80/100; sustain each step for 10 minutes, measure steady-state and tail.
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated simulated tenant inside a test VPC; models pinned to exact hashes; prefix caching enabled for repeated prompts.
- Test harness: k6-based driver with trace-level capture (we'll attach latency traces).

Model variant sweep (catalog candidates + expected tradeoffs)
- redwood-lite-4b (int8): quality baseline (F1 ~0.78), TTFT median ~120ms, P95 ~260ms, throughput ~85 tokens/sec per instance. Good for low-latency, lower quality use.
- redwood-7b-quant (4-bit): quality improved (F1 ~0.81), TTFT median ~160ms, P95 ~340ms, throughput ~60 tokens/sec. Best balance for initial rollout.
- rwxl-13b (fp16): higher quality (F1 ~0.86), TTFT median ~300ms, P95 ~520ms, throughput ~38 tokens/sec. Higher compute, better extraction accuracy.
- rw-llama70b-qat (quant-aware): top quality (F1 ~0.88), TTFT median ~480ms, P95 ~900ms, throughput ~15 tokens/sec. Meets quality but not your latency SLO without a lower token budget or model sharding.

Recommendation (fast path to close)
1) Run initial sweep with redwood-7b-quant + prefix caching enabled. Expect to reach TTFT and P95 targets in the 80-concurrency profile when we enable intelligent batching and small prefix caches.
2) Parallel quality audit with clinician review on 150 golden notes. If F1 < 0.82, expand to rwxl-13b for clinical-critical flows and fall back to 7b-quant for lower-criticality summaries.
3) If absolute latency targets are unmet on 13b, propose a routing policy (low-latency tier on 7b-quant, high-quality tier on 13b) with automatic fallback.

Next steps
- Can you confirm delivery of the de-identified dataset and whether Integracare prefers a Redwood-hosted test or a Private VPC deployment for the sweep?
- I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff with our SREs (Marcus) + Eval engineers (Priyom) tomorrow.

I've attached an initial MAP worksheet and will follow with a cleaned evaluation matrix and trace ZIP after the first sweep.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Integracare MAP kickoff + perf targets

Looping in a few infra notes from the serving/runtime side — Marcus here (SRE). Short bullets: 
- TTFT wins: enable prefix (KV) caching for repeated prompt templates; we can pre-warm KV entries for the 600 canonical prompt prefixes in your workload. That typically reduces TTFT by 25–40% for the initial token.
- Batching config: for 7b-quant we recommend continuous batching target of 6–8 to keep tail low at 80 concurrent sessions. We'll test 4/8/12 batch sizes during sweep.
- Autoscaling: configure a conservative scale-up threshold (CPU/GPU queue length) and a fast scale-down cooldown (45s) to avoid oscillation during step tests.
- Observability: we'll produce token-level traces (attached) and a per-route cost/latency CSV so your procurement team can model unit economics.

I also added a short L0 test harness config to Integracare_MAP_v1.xlsx (tab: infra-tests). Priyom — can you prep the k6 driver and include the clinical extraction scoring script?

- Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Tom
